subject: Clarifying commit tiers & marketplace pass-through impact on Hosted API discounts
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying commit tiers & marketplace pass-through impact on Hosted API discounts

Hi Liam — great talking yesterday. Thanks for outlining Acme's anticipated usage trajectory for Q1/Q2 next year. Per our conversation I wanted to follow up with a concise summary of how commits and marketplace billing interact so your procurement team can evaluate economics quickly.

Key points up front: 
- Hosted API discounts are applied to usage based on an agreed committed spend or token-volume tier.
- Marketplace billing (AWS/GCP/Azure) introduces a platform fee and activation method ("pass-through") that typically reduces the effective discount we can offer compared with a direct invoiced commit.
- There are two practical paths we see customers use: a) Direct Redwood contract with commit tiers (max discount flexibility), or b) Marketplace billing where we mirror tiers but account for marketplace fees — usually a steeper list discount is needed to achieve a similar net-of-fees price.

I've attached a short XLS that models a few scenarios (monthly token volumes, list price, marketplace fee assumptions). Can you confirm if procurement prefers a contract that must go through AWS Marketplace or if they can accept a direct Red­wood invoice? That will materially change the commitment structure we propose.

Next steps: if marketplace is required, Neha can walk you through our marketplace tier mapping and Ben can run the net pricing table. If direct is an option, we can draft a straightforward commit amendment and start a 30-day SOW review.

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

---

On Mon, 2 Nov 2026 at 08:33 AM, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-analytics.com> wrote:
> Jordan — thanks for the overview and the modeling file. A couple of clarifying questions from procurement and finance: 
> 
> 1) If we route through AWS Marketplace, do we still get the same SLA and dedicated egress protections, or does that change?
> 2) How do you calculate the marketplace "pass-through" impact — is it a fixed platform fee or a percentage we should factor into our forecasts?
> 3) Our legal prefers a single-contract model via marketplace for all cloud spend — is there a hybrid approach that keeps things simple for us while preserving some level of Redwood discount?
> 
> Happy to jump on a short call this week.
> 
> — Liam

On Mon, 2 Nov 2026 at 09:02 AM, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Liam — looping in Neha (sales lead on this deal) and Ben (finance/pricing) so they can give concrete numbers. Short answers: 
> - SLA/features: unchanged for functional SLAs and dedicated capacity clauses; procurement still needs to accept the marketplace terms around billing and tax handling. Security controls (KMS, VPC) are unchanged operationally.
> - Marketplace impact: typically a % fee (varies by marketplace) + payment processing timing effects; we'll quantify with Ben.
> - Hybrid: we can do a marketplace entry (for your contract rules) and a side letter or rebate that nets to a similar economic outcome, but that requires a longer legal review and usually an acceptance of an escrow/attestation.
> 
> Ben & Neha — can you review the attached and add a net-pricing example for both direct invoice vs AWS Marketplace pass-through? If the marketplace fee is 8-12% (typical) we will need to adjust list discounts to match Acme's target per-token net cost.
> 
> Jordan

--

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying commit tiers & marketplace pass-through impact on Hosted API discounts

Jordan / Neha / Liam — reviewed the model. A few concrete notes from finance: 

- Marketplace pass-through mechanics: AWS Marketplace charges a fee that is either a percentage of the gross or a fixed platform cut depending on the SKU and program (private offers can change this). For modeling, assume 10% effective marketplace fee for initial calc; we can refine with AWS partner team.

- Effective discount math (simple example):
  * List price per token = $0.0006
  * Direct commit discount (annual): 30% => net $0.00042
  * If routed via marketplace with 10% fee, Redwood receives 90% of customer payment; to achieve the same $0.00042 net to Redwood we'd need to offer the customer a roughly 33.3% list discount (because 0.9 * price_after_discount = 0.00042). That increases visible discount on paperwork even though net to Redwood is equivalent.

- Commit tiers: we recommend 3 tiers for Acme's expected volumes (monthly avg tokens): Bronze (0-500M), Silver (500M-2B), Gold (2B+). Each tier maps to a target annual commit and an escalating discount curve. Markets often demand an explicit mapping for marketplace SKUs — that adds governance overhead.

- Hybrid/legal: we can offer a marketplace private offer + direct-side rebate executed after payment (monthly reconciliation). Legal review takes ~2–3 weeks. If Acme needs single-contract marketplace-only, we can still reach an acceptable net price but list discounts will look larger on marketplace invoices.

Attached: RI_commit_table_v3.xlsx (two tabs: direct_net_example, marketplace_net_example).

Ben
Finance — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying commit tiers & marketplace pass-through impact on Hosted API discounts

Liam — thanks; based on Ben's model I'm proposing we offer two commercial paths for Acme to discuss internally: 

Option A — Direct Redwood Commit (preferred):
- Annual commit: $360K (apportioned monthly)
- Gold tier pricing on tokens (net 30% off list)
- Simpler legal timeline (~1 week for standard SOW + order form)
- Full visibility in Redwood Console, token-level billing, and standard SLA.

Option B — AWS Marketplace Private Offer + Rebate (procurement-friendly):
- Public-facing discount ~34% (to account for ~10% marketplace fee); Redwood receives net equivalent to Option A after fee.
- Requires temporary private-offer creation in AWS and monthly reconciliation to apply any side-letter rebate.
- Legal timeline ~3 weeks due to private offer and rebate language.

If procurement needs vendor consolidation to marketplace only, Option B is workable; otherwise Option A is simpler and quicker to activate. Which would procurement prefer? If you give the go-ahead I can prepare draft paperwork for either path.

Best — Jordan

--

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-analytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, AWS Partner Sales <aws-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying commit tiers & marketplace pass-through impact on Hosted API discounts

Jordan / team — thanks, that framing is exactly what procurement needed. Acme legal is going to prefer the marketplace private offer route for centralization reasons, but they asked that we keep any rebate mechanism as automated and auditable as possible. Please: 

1) Share the AWS private-offer flow and timeline (AWS team, can you confirm typical turn-around?)
2) Send a sample private-offer + side-letter language we can use as a starting point so our counsel can review.
> Attachment: Please include the XLS with the marketplace net example on top — procurement asked for that in the review.

If we can get private offer paperwork by next week, we'll escalate to approvals. Appreciate the clear options.

— Liam

On Thu, 5 Nov 2026 at 17:12:00 -0700, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai> wrote:

Ben — can you produce the side-letter template and a short reconciliation cadence note (monthly ledger + proof of payment) by EOD tomorrow?
> 
> Jordan
